subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Hi Alex —

Great to meet you on the call today. Per our discussion, sharing a quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can align on a target price per 1M tokens for your evaluation: 

Summary from call:
- Expected monthly token volume: 200M inference tokens, 50M embedding tokens (estimates)
- Current target budget range: $10k–$30k / month (finance still finalizing)
- Production latency SLOs: 100–200ms p50 for text generation; embeddings can be higher latency
- Primary comparison models: OpenAI (gpt-4o/embeddings), Anthropic, and self-hosted/hosted open models via other hosts

Key ask for next step: can you confirm the breakdown of 1) average prompt+completion token ratio for the generation calls, and 2) whether the 200M tokens is purely inference (not counting internal caching hits)? That will help us map to $/1M token unit economics.

Attached: rough token-volume worksheet (acme-token-usage-estimates.csv) and a sample price comparison template I’ll fill once you confirm ratios.

Target next steps:
1) Alex to confirm token ratios and any hard budget constraints by Mon 8/10
2) Vanessa/Marissa to return a target $/1M token benchmarking table (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic/hosted open-models) by Tue 8/11
3) Schedule procurement sync if the numbers look good

Thanks — enjoyed the product conversation.
—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
(415) 555-0187

Attachment: acme-token-usage-estimates.csv (CSV stub: monthly_token_type,estimated_monthly_tokens)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Thanks Vanessa — good recap. Quick answers below: 

- Prompt vs completion ratio: for our main assistant flow average prompt is ~60 tokens, completion average ~140 tokens (so ~200 tokens per request).
- The 200M inference tokens estimate includes both prompt+completion. Embedding calls (50M) are separate and we count each embedding as ~512 tokens equivalent in your worksheet.
- The volume estimate does not attempt to include cache hits; some traffic will hit prefix cache but we assume worst-case for budgeting.
- Finance: target spend ceiling is $25k/month for the pilot, but they would prefer hitting economics at $10k–$15k/month if possible.

Also attaching our procurement guide (see Procure-ACME.pdf) — procurement will want a line item for $/1M tokens and an estimate for monthly committed spend.

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min call next week if you want to walk through the numbers.

- Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of AI Platforms | Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Alex — this helps a lot. Based on the 200 tokens/request and your volumes, our rough mapping: 

- Generation tokens: 200M tokens/month -> ~1M requests/month (200 tokens/req)
- Embeddings: 50M tokens/month treated as 50M embedding units for now

Preliminary target $/1M token benchmarking (ballpark, subject to confirmation on model family/throughput):
- OpenAI equivalent: $45–$60 per 1M tokens (depending on model, embeddings priced separately)
- Anthropic equivalent: $35–$55 per 1M tokens
- Hosted open-model providers (varies by instance/quantization/throughput): $12–$28 per 1M tokens
- Redwood (target/compressed pricing for pilot commit + batching/kv-cache gains): $9–$20 per 1M tokens depending on model and committed volume

Notes:
- Hosted open-model providers can sometimes achieve lower list $/1M tokens but with higher variability and less predictable latency; many do not include managed KV cache or production-grade fallbacks.
- Redwood pricing above factors in expected batching gains and prefix/KV cache for assistant flows — effective $/1M can be lower if cache hit rate improves.

Action items from us:
- Marissa to produce the formal benchmarking table with model assumptions and per-1M token line items by Tue EOD (included in attached PDF).
- Vanessa to propose a pilot pricing band for Acme: $9–$12 per 1M tokens for the first 3 months on a 6-month reserved pilot, then re-evaluate.

Can you confirm whether procurement needs a single blended $/1M token line or separate lines for generation vs embeddings? Procurement usually prefers a single easy-to-compare line item, but engineering cares about per-call unit economics.

If that sounds right I’ll have Marissa draft the formal comparison and a pilot proposal.
—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Hi Alex — looping in the benchmarking table and assumptions (attached as 20260810-acme-benchmarking.pdf). Quick highlights in-line: 

- Assumptions: generation model family = open-opt-6.9b equivalent for hosted open-model hosts; OpenAI comparators use gpt-4o pricing bands; Anthropic uses Claude-2 equivalent bands. Embedding unit conversions shown in the PDF.
- Per-1M token guidance (final numbers in table):
  - OpenAI: $48 / 1M tokens (midpoint of $45–$60)
  - Anthropic: $46 / 1M tokens (midpoint of $35–$55)
  - Hosted open-models: $20 / 1M tokens (typical mid-market for managed hosts with quantization)
  - Redwood (pilot reserved band): $10 / 1M tokens (with a 6-month reserved pilot + caching enabled; price scales down with higher commit)

Procurement recommendation: provide a blended generation+embedding line for initial comparison ($/1M tokens) and an appendix that shows separate lines and assumptions so engineering can validate. That satisfies the procurement request while keeping contract comparability simple.

Next steps: 
- Vanessa: send pilot commercial (terms + $10/1M tokens at 6-month reserve) to procurement and scheduling a call with procurement.
- Alex: confirm procurement preference for blended vs split by Tue 8/11 so we can finalize the proposal.

Thanks — attaching the benchmarking PDF and the filled token worksheet.
—
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: 20260810-acme-benchmarking.pdf, acme-token-usage-estimates-filled.csv
